item.title: AI in Portfolio Management: A Tool, Not a Decision Maker
item.description: By grounding portfolio management in strong data foundations, clear decision ownership and well-defined analytical pillars, insurers can apply AI in a targeted way that reinforces judgment, improves governance and accelerates action rather than replacing it. (Image source: IIR.) Portfolio management is a critical discipline for P&C insurers seeking sustainable profitability in an increasingly complex market. Done well, portfolio management enables data-driven decisions that protect margins and guide growth, even when data is imperfect.

item.title: NYC Officials Feared Liability Over Toxic Air After 9/11 Attacks
item.description: 11, 2001, attacks, including documents showing officials were weighing potential liability from toxic exposure while trying to reassure the public about the safety of Lower Manhattan. One memo prepared in October 2001 for Robert Harding, a deputy mayor under Rudy Guiliani, estimated that the city could face 35,000 potential plaintiffs and contemplated seeking federal protection from “toxic tort cases that might arise in the next few decades.” Another city document from May 2002 said that officials would avoid using the word “risk” in correspondence about a cleanup program because doing so “would defeat the purpose of creating public confidence.” An estimated 400,000 people, including first responders, were exposed to toxic contaminants and other hazards in the days, weeks and months following the attacks, according to the CDC. Fires in the towers’ debris piles burned for months after the attacks, releasing carcinogenic byproducts.

item.title: Retrocession set for comeback as conditions evolve. Collateralized tail protection stable: S&P
item.description: Retrocession is back in fashion as market conditions evolve across reinsurance and rating agency S&P believes retro buying is set for a comeback, as reinsurers recognise favourable pricing and conditions for protection, while looking to manage their catastrophe limits in a softening market. S&P said that “retrocession is set for a comeback as market conditions evolve.” As of January 1st 2026, S&P’s benchmark reinsurance group on average ceded roughly 50% of their exposure to a 1-in-250 year event. “Reinsurers that successfully balance growth ambitions with risk mitigation will be well positioned to protect capital strength and navigate the next phase of the reinsurance cycle.” But, despite this capital strength across the reinsurance sector, S&P also notes that reinsurers recognise the opportunity to benefit from softening market conditions to further build their protection through retrocession purchases.

item.title: Industry loss estimate for Saskatchewan and Manitoba severe weather reaches CAD 923m: CatIQ
item.description: CatIQ, the independent Toronto-based catastrophe insurance data provider and subsidiary of PERILS, has revised its industry loss estimate for the severe storm outbreak in Saskatchewan and Manitoba, Canada, to CAD 923 million. The severe weather event took place between June 9 and 10, impacting the Saskatchewan and Manitoba provinces which experienced heavy storms that brought tornadoes, hail, damaging winds, torrential rain and flash flooding, affecting tens of thousands of residents and businesses. Laura Twidle, President and CEO of CatIQ, commented: “Canada experienced severe weather-related loss events at an above-average pace in the summer of 2026.

item.title: Bamboo Insurance Launches Texas Homeowner Program
item.description: Bamboo Insurance announced the launch of its Texas Essential Homeowner Program, a new admitted, flexible product designed to give Texas homeowners greater flexibility in how they structure their coverage. Bamboo Insurance said the structure keeps coverage transparent while providing greater flexibility to insureds to tailor coverage to their individual needs and budgets. The launch builds on Bamboo Insurance’s continued expansion of its product offerings and capacity.

item.title: Higginbotham Acquires Kansas’ Two West Capital Advisors
item.description: Higginbotham announced it has acquired Kansas City, Kansas-based Two West Capital Advisors. Two West will remain based in Kansas City and continue serving its existing clients, with all current teammates on board — and new ones coming in as the firm actively recruits for expected growth. That team will gain the support of Higginbotham’s broader HR, marketing, legal and compliance infrastructure, while Two West employees also become employee-owners in the larger organization.

item.title: Illinois Sues Repair Company for Deceptive Business Practices
item.description: (ABC) for its deceptive business practices that mislead consumers, most often senior citizens, to sign a contract for home repair work at inflated prices by unlicensed technicians while they also unknowingly waive their statutory rights to cancel the contract. Raoul’s lawsuit claims ABC violates the Illinois Consumer Fraud Act, Deceptive Trade Practices Act and the Illinois Home Repair and Remodeling Act. Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul last week filed a lawsuit against ABC Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Electric, Inc.

item.title: Allstate Trains Adjusters in Damaged Homes
item.description: Source: Allstate.) Allstate (Northbrook, Ill.) has built two full-scale homes inside its Claims University training center to help property claim adjusters learn how residential damage occurs, spreads and is repaired. Allstate says the homes include standard-grade components and higher-end materials to help adjusters prepare for varied property conditions and repair considerations. The homes recreate residential damage scenarios that adjusters may encounter when helping homeowners recover from property damage.

item.title: Singapore’s DBS Faces $1 Billion Lawsuit in Alleged 1MDB-Linked Claim
item.description: DBS Bank is being sued for an estimated S$1.298 billion ($1.03 billion) in damages linked to the multibillion-dollar 1MDB scandal, Southeast Asia’s largest lender DBS Group said on Wednesday. In July last year, liquidators trying to recover money from 1MDB sued Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore, alleging it enabled fraud that led to more than $2.7 billion in financial losses between 2009 and 2013. DBS rejected the claim and said it would fight it vigorously, adding that the company has made no provision for the lawsuit.

item.title: Probe Underway in Deadly Amazon Cargo Jet’s Fiery Runway Crash
item.description: The five people killed when an Amazon cargo jet ran off a runway at Miami International Airport were all inside a van carrying seven people from a cleaning company, and an SUV hit outside of airport property, National Transportation Safety Board Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said Monday. Homendy called the scene of Sunday’s crash “utter devastation.” She didn’t detail how many people were in the SUV or where the dead were located. Federal investigators examining cause of deadly overrun

item.title: Despite Security Concerns, Meta Launches AI Agent Muse
item.description: Meta rolled out on Tuesday a long-touted AI assistant that can autonomously send emails, sell a car and book travel on a person’s behalf, despite internal concerns that the technology mismanages its access to sensitive personal data. The company’s Muse agent, known internally as Hatch, is the centerpiece of CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s plan to supply “personal superintelligence” to the billions of people who use Meta’s services daily. Modeled on the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, Muse is designed to access a person’s apps across categories like email, calendar, payments, health, shopping and the smart home, Meta said.

item.title: New York Staged Crash Ringleaders Sentenced
item.description: A ringleader and co-conspirator were sentenced to prison time last month for orchestrating crashes on New York highways in 2024, according to a joint press release issued by Governor Kathy Hochul and Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz. The staged crashes occurred on the following dates: Defendants Maikel Martinez and Ivon Matus-Martinez, alleged participants in the crashes, also pled guilty and are expected to be sentenced next month. The two Brooklyn-based men were found guilty of charges related to staging three crashes on New York City highways and seeking fraudulent insurance payouts for damages and injuries.

item.title: The Sales Test This Norwest Partner Gives Founders Before He’ll Invest
item.description: He later became a venture partner at Emergence Capital before joining Norwest in 2014. As a partner at Menlo Park, California-based venture firm Norwest, Jacobsohn focuses on enterprise software, drawing on his background in finance, sales and business development. In an interview with Crunchbase News, Jacobsohn discusses where he still sees openings in the crowded market for finance software, how far companies should trust AI with accounting work, why HR startups may be better off attacking the secondary products of large platforms, and why he tests a CEO’s sales ability before investing.

item.title: Catastrophe bond market coupon falls 4.5% in August, now 13% lower than a year ago: Plenum
item.description: “The seasonal spread tightening is in full swing, with an average market yield of 5.05% as of end of August.” Further noting that, “The market yield has now reached 2020 levels, highlighting one more time the softening of the market.” Click the chart below to analyse the interactive data : It’s worth noting that a year ago the overall coupon of the catastrophe bond market according to this data set stood at 10.22%, some 13% higher that today. During August 2026 catastrophe bond seasonal spread tightening accelerated and as a result the catastrophe bond market yield , or coupon available to investors, fell around 4.5% in the month. Which leaves it now 13% lower than it was at the same time last year, according to the latest data on cat bond yields from Plenum Investments.

item.title: Casualty ILS needs to demonstrate discipline through market cycles to attract capital: MultiStrat CUO
item.description: Speaking with Artemis at the 2026 Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous, Kier James, Chief Underwriting Officer (CUO) of MultiStrat, underscored that as the casualty insurance-linked securities (ILS) market continues to grow, it also needs to demonstrate that it can be disciplined throughout market cycles in order to continue attracting capital and build confidence with investors. “I think casualty ILS needs also to demonstrate that it can be disciplined throughout market cycles in order to continue to attract capital and build confidence with investors,” James added. However, as casualty ILS continues to grow, maintaining market discipline is going to be one of the biggest challenges going forward, James highlighted to Artemis.

item.title: Data centre opportunity for ILS capital must be effective in terms of the economics: Swiss Re
item.description: When it comes to alternative sources of reinsurance capital and insurance-linked securities (ILS) investors supporting the massive need for capacity to insure and reinsure the data centre build-out, Swiss Re executives explained in Monte Carlo that it must be effective in terms of the economics. With the reinsurance industry meeting in Monte Carlo at the 2026 Rendez-vous event, Swiss Re held a briefing focused on its recent research into the data centre risk transfer opportunity. As we reported, Swiss Re Institute’s report highlights a potential US$200 billion premium opportunity by 2030 from data centres and related renewable energy infrastructure, within which it sees alternative reinsurance capital, including catastrophe bonds and sidecars, as likely to play a key role .

item.title: Oxbow Partners’ Sandilands says reinsurers must transition to ‘small big companies’
item.description: Speaking to Reinsurance News at Rendez-Vous de Septembre in Monte Carlo 2026, Chris Sandilands, Partner at Oxbow Partners, the insurance and reinsurance-focused strategy consultancy, discussed the January renewals, the state of artificial intelligence adoption across the market, and what he believes separates reinsurers building lasting advantage from those simply riding favourable conditions. On rate movements at the January 1 renewals, Sandilands said “The overall direction of travel is clearly downwards, although I think it is important not to reduce the market to a single headline number.” He noted that “the headline index people tend to focus on is property catastrophe, but that is only one part of the overall reinsurance market.” According to Sandilands, “one of the more interesting data points from Monte Carlo was Munich Re’s commentary, which suggested that property cat is a relatively small part of the broader story,” adding that “other lines of business appear much more stable, even if there are clear areas of pressure.” Even so, Sandilands pointed to “meaningful pull-backs across the market”, citing figures showing “RenRe, for example, cut its top line by 12.5% year-on-year in Q2, while Munich Re and Swiss Re were both down around 10% in P&C reinsurance.” He said “that suggests there is still some discipline in the market.” At the same time, he observed that “many clients are talking about ‘pockets of opportunity’,” explaining that “some of these will be areas where reinsurers defend existing business hard; others may be genuine opportunities to write new business,” and that “as some players reduce exposure to areas such as US casualty, they will inevitably look for growth elsewhere to protect volumes.” Sandilands said “the question, from a strategy perspective, is whether those opportunities are truly attractive or whether they are partly the result of looser assumptions and optimism.” As he put it, “in theory, time will tell. In practice, European reinsurers have built up significant reserve buffers over the past two to three years, which means some underwriting under-performance could be masked in the P&L for the next year or two.” Turning to artificial intelligence, Sandilands said: “AI is both fascinating and difficult to pin down because it is such a broad topic.” He observed: “You would think that a technology powerful enough to concern governments about cyber and infrastructure risk would be able to transform treaty underwriting, yet many reinsurers are still working through submission ingestion and underwriting workflow automation.” According to Sandilands, “the reality is that many reinsurers will privately say they are either still at an early stage of AI adoption or are struggling to scale it meaningfully.” He said that “over the past 18 months, we have seen a proliferation of proofs of concept and experiments,” adding that “in that sense, the AI cycle has some similarities with the InsurTech cycle ten years ago: there was a rush to experiment, a lot of bold claims, and then a more difficult journey to turn activity into real value or structural change.” Sandilands said genuine progress today is visible in “relatively practical use cases: submission ingestion, triage, claims processing and other process-heavy activities.” He noted these “can deliver real efficiencies, but we think many of these benefits will commoditise over time.” For Sandilands, “the more interesting question is how AI changes the operating model,” meaning “moving beyond narrow technology pilots and asking how the business itself should be organised to create value from AI.” He said: “We are seeing less progress on building multi-disciplinary teams that bring together underwriters, data specialists and AI experts to create differentiating capability,” adding that “in some ways, that is similar to how hedge funds brought trading strategy and quantitative skills closer together.”

item.title: Domus PTA to support DARAG’s continued expansion across Nordic region
item.description: “We are delighted to partner with Domus on its planned exit from the Danish insurance market and to combine DARAG’s financial strength and run-off expertise with established local claims management capabilities to provide long-term certainty for policyholders, claimants and other stakeholders.” The deal marks another milestone in DARAG’s continued expansion across the Nordic region, reinforcing its commitment to providing innovative run-off solutions across Europe. Legacy acquirer DARAG Group has announced that it has entered into a portfolio transfer agreement (PTA) with Domus Forsikring A/S, for its entire change of ownership (Husejerskifte) and building damage (Byggeskade) portfolio in Denmark. Pending standard regulatory approvals, the transaction will allow Domus, a Danish property and casualty insurance company, to fully resolve these liabilities, exit the insurance market and ultimately wind up the company.

item.title: Orion180 seeks to raise up to $340m in IPO
item.description: Orion180 Insurance, a founder-led, technology-focused, high-growth, high-margin specialty insurance group, has launched the roadshow for its proposed US initial public offering, seeking to raise $300 million to $340 million in gross proceeds from the sale of 20 million Class A shares priced at $15 to $17 each. The Florida-based specialty insurer could raise a further $45 million to $51 million if underwriters exercise their full 30-day option to purchase an additional 3 million shares, which would bring total gross proceeds to $345 million-$391 million. Orion180 said the net proceeds will primarily be used to increase capitalisation and financial flexibility and provide capital to grow the business, while a portion could be used to repay borrowings under its new credit facility.

item.title: SEC Seeks Court Order for ISS Client Data Sought in ESG Probe
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission asked a federal court for an order compelling Institutional Shareholder Services Inc. to turn over detailed client-level voting data requested by the agency as part of an investigation into the proxy advisory firm. “It is wholly appropriate for the SEC to look into whether ISS’s investment advice to clients on proxy voting is driven by a particular political or policy aim to the detriment of its clients’ interests,” the SEC said in Friday’s filing, which seeks records from the advisory firm over a period of four years, including documents identifying clients and voting data.

item.title: Feathery launches Robin AI operations assistant for insurance and financial services
item.description: The post Feathery launches Robin AI operations assistant for insurance and financial services appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Feathery  has launched  Robin , an artificial intelligence operations assistant designed to enable insurers, wealth managers and banks to build and modify operational workflows using natural-language instructions. One RIA launched an entirely new onboarding experience in a week connected to their systems: work that takes months with a traditional vendor-built approach.” The launch expands Feathery’s use of AI across financial services operations, with its platform designed to automate workflows spanning data, documents, decisions and actions for insurers, wealth managers and banks.

item.description: Ivans ® today announced the August 2026 results of the Ivans Index , the insurance industry’s premium renewal rate index. Released monthly, Ivans Index is a data-driven report of current conditions and trends for premium rate renewal change of the most placed commercial lines of business in the insurance industry. Download the complete Q2 2026 Ivans Index report .

item.title: Markel launches clinical trial travel coverage
item.description: The coverage reimburses trial sponsors for eligible expenses associated with international travel by registered participants to and from clinical trial sites. Markel International has launched a travel reimbursement enhancement for life sciences companies and other sponsors conducting rare-disease clinical trials. The product is available through brokers and is designed to address gaps in traditional travel insurance, which may exclude preexisting conditions or travel undertaken to participate in a clinical trial.

item.title: Conning Report: Turning MGA Growth into Staying Power
item.description: For the past several years, the MGA story has been one of growth, and that trend appears to be continuing with Conning’s 2026 report showing a 12% year-over-year premium growth from 2024 to 2025. It’s here where operational maturity and a strong technology partner can help secure the value MGAs have enjoyed in recent years, turning the surge of recent growth into long-term performance at scale. However, Conning’s report also raises important questions about the viability of such growth and whether the market will settle toward MGAs, carriers, or a coexistence between the two.

item.title: Judge Says Smucker’s Suit Against Trader Joe’s Over Frozen PB&J Can Proceed
item.description: Smucker can proceed with a lawsuit against Trader Joe’s over frozen sandwiches that Smucker claims are too similar to its Uncrustables. Smucker sued Trader Joe’s in federal court in Ohio last fall, claiming Trader Joe’s committed a trademark violation when it introduced frozen peanut butter and jelly sandwiches with the same round shape and crimped edges as Uncrustables. District Judge John Adams ruled Friday that Smucker had devoted significant resources to developing Uncrustables and protecting the brand over the past 20 years.

item.title: Deutsche Bank And Former Banker Settle $176M Lawsuit for Undisclosed Sum
item.description: Deutsche Bank said it has settled a lawsuit with a second former employee who sought damages in a case involving business with Italy’s Monte dei Paschi, days ahead of a trial that threatened to embroil the bank’s CEO. It was the second settlement in the dispute, leaving the cases of the four other former Deutsche Bank staff who are claiming more than 600 million pounds ($812.16 million) in a London court. The bank has now settled with two of the six former employees who filed the suits.

item.title: The Causation Gap: Why Workers’ Comp Files Stall and What Changes It
item.description: View Series A workers’ comp story claims professionals know all too well — and what’s finally changing it. With caseloads in workers’ comp commonly running between 110 and 140 open files per examiner , and research suggesting that anything over 125 can increase the cost of a claim by up to 20% , the math simply doesn’t work. Fragmented across dozens of documents , duplicated across providers, and contradicted between a treating physician’s note from month two and an IME report from month eight, manual review of a complex workers’ comp file takes days.

Eckert joins Willis Re from Bermuda-based reinsurer Conduit Re, which he co-founded in 2020. Eckert will take up his position at Willis Re after completing his existing contractual commitments.

item.title: Discipline matters more than growth, right-sizing ILS capital is key: Parry, RenaissanceRe
item.description: In this insurance-linked securities market environment where engagement from investors remains strong, Chris Parry, the Global Head of RenaissanceRe Capital Partners told us that a disciplined approach matters more than growth and right-sizing capital is key at this stage of the reinsurance cycle. Parry feels that ensuring capital is right-sized to the opportunity is critical in disciplined ILS management and this is a key feature of ILS manager discipline at this time. “In our view, protecting underwriting margins and delivering strong returns for our investors over the long-term is far more important than growing assets under management,” Parry explained.

item.title: US P&C underwriting gains improved in H1’26, but performance varied by line of business and geography: Verisk
item.description: US property and casualty (P&C) insurers have posted strong underwriting gains of $31.7 billion through the first half of 2026, up from the $11.6 billion recorded through midyear 2025, according to Verisk and the American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA) data, yet line-specific and geographic challenges persist. Saurabh Khemka, president of Verisk Underwriting Solutions, stated: “First-half results should not be mistaken as evidence that underlying risk has diminished. Broader industry performance highlights the growing value of precision as property market conditions continue to soften.

item.title: Reinsurance industry normalising after exceptionally strong period: BCG
item.description: Boston Consulting Group (BCG) analysts have said the reinsurance industry is normalising after an “exceptionally strong period” of improving pricing, robust returns, and rapid balance-sheet growth, in its new 2026 Insurance Value Creators Report. The report also affirmed that reinsurance remains a strong long-term value creator, generating an average annual TSR of 13.4% over the ten years from 2016 through 2025. Over the five years through 2025, reinsurance generated average annual total shareholder returns (TSR) of 19.1%, but one-year TSR fell sharply from 29% in 2024 to 14% in 2025, albeit still above the 10-year average.

Wholesale on-peak power prices in Southern California’s SP15 hub, which includes the Los Angeles metropolitan area, rose as high as $87.69 a megawatt-hour for 6 p.m. Most power being used today was contracted the prior day in the day-ahead market based on demand forecasts.

item.title: Amazon Accused in Lawsuit of Systematic Discrimination Against Pregnant Employees
item.description: The lawsuit seeks lost pay and benefits, punitive damages, and an injunction against discrimination against pregnant employees. 8 in a proposed nationwide class action accusing the retailer of systematically discriminating against thousands of pregnant employees, including by firing some it claimed took too much time off. According to a complaint filed by four former warehouse employees, Amazon routinely violates federal and New York worker-protection laws by denying pregnant workers basic accommodations such as chairs, bathroom and water breaks, and time off for prenatal appointments.

item.title: Trump Administration Stalled a Survey of PFAS in Wastewater, Former EPA Officials Say

A public notice shows the first of its kind survey of wastewater treatment plants was submitted to the White House for approval nearly two years ago during the Biden administration — a far longer wait than is typical. The Trump administration’s nuanced — and at times controversial — stance towards PFAS The Trump administration has promised to combat PFAS.
